subject: Use cast to get wide format

messages.author: a7dfc51fb83e93ca
messages.subject: Use cast to get wide format
parts:
Hi, everyone,
I have used cast to transform long format into wide format, but in
one case it does not work. It is:

library(MASS)
data(coop)
cast(coop, Spc + Bat ~ Lab, value="Conc")

Aggregation requires fun.aggregate: length used as default
Spc Bat L1 L2 L3 L4 L5 L6
1 S1 B1 2 2 2 2 2 2
2 S1 B2 2 2 2 2 2 2
3 S1 B3 2 2 2 2 2 2
4 S2 B1 2 2 2 2 2 2
5 S2 B2 2 2 2 2 2 2
6 S2 B3 2 2 2 2 2 2
......

But this is not what I want. I have used function reshape:

reshape(coop,v.names="Conc",timevar="Lab",idvar=c("Spc","Bat"),
direction="wide")

Spc Bat Conc.L1 Conc.L2 Conc.L3 Conc.L4 Conc.L5 Conc.L6
1 S1 B1 0.29 0.40 0.40 0.9 0.44 0.38
3 S1 B2 0.33 0.43 0.38 0.9 0.45 0.40
5 S1 B3 0.34 0.42 0.38 0.9 0.42 0.72
7 S2 B1 0.13 0.22 0.25 1.7 0.23 0.24
9 S2 B2 0.16 0.24 0.16 1.5 0.22 0.15
11 S2 B3 0.14 0.21 0.25 0.6 0.24 0.35
.......

It is the exactly what I want.

Could someone tell me what wrong with my cast application?

Many thanks in advance.

WLL

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Use cast to get wide format
parts:
Your cast() indicated the number of observations in each cell. To put
it another way, try

with(coop, table(Lab, Spc, Bat))

Also look at the row numbers of your reshape() output. If you want to
cast the data, you will need to define a function for the
fun.aggregate = argument. That's what Hadley is telling you without
explicitly telling you :)

Dennis
